observations: Photo 0: a yellow steel cooking gas cylinder with a protective collar, faded paint, scuffs and dark spots, handwritten marker figures on the shoulder and an old gas-shop sticker with phone numbers on the collar.
Photo 0: stamped markings on the collar are present but too faint to read, so tare weight, capacity and test date cannot be read.

Photos 1 and 2: a different cylinder, blue, with a globe logo whose text is only partly legible; the collar rim is worn black with chipped paint and rust spots, and the valve is a bare brass outlet with no regulator.
The yellow and blue cylinders are clearly two separate items, both visibly used.
Proportions of both, roughly twice as tall as wide, are consistent with the common 12.5kg household size, but no stamped capacity is legible.
Watermark 'PETRONJAY BUSINESS' and 'POSTED ON' text on all photos, so this is a trader's listing.

claims.evidence: Shape in photos 0 to 2 fits the 12.5kg size, but the stamped capacity on the collar in photo 0 is unreadable and the blue cylinder's stamp is not shown.
Photo 0 shows faded paint, scuffs and marker writing; photos 1 and 2 show a worn, chipped and rusty collar rim.
Valve seat and welds are not shown close up; no test record shown.
No leak test or pressure check shown; valve condition unknown.
No receipt or warranty shown; a used cylinder from a trader normally has none.

risks.proof: Close, sharp photo of the stamped tare weight and water capacity on the collar.
risks.if_unproven: as a used cylinder of the size seen, at the low end of the 12.5kg range

risks.risk: Valve leaks or is damaged; cylinder will not hold gas.
risks.proof: Clip of a soapy water leak test on the valve with the cylinder filled.

risks.risk: Cylinder is past its hydrostatic test date or has internal corrosion, making it unsafe to refill.
risks.proof: Close photo of the stamped manufacture or last test date on the collar.
risks.if_unproven: as out of test, needing requalification

risks.risk: Dents or rust at the base, foot ring or weld seams not shown.
risks.proof: Photo of the cylinder tipped to show the base and foot ring.

risks.risk: Unclear which cylinder is on sale; photos show two different ones.
risks.proof: Seller confirmation plus a photo of the exact cylinder offered with a handwritten note bearing today's date.
risks.if_unproven: as one cylinder, the more worn blue one

proof_requests: Close photo of the stamped tare weight, capacity and test date on the collar.
Confirmation of which cylinder is for sale, with a dated note in the photo.
Clip of a soapy water leak test on the valve.
Photo of the base and foot ring.
response.reason: Photos 0 to 2 show used household cooking gas cylinders whose shape fits the 12.5kg size, so one can be priced by type at its worst case, worn, out of test and with an unproven valve, until the stamped markings and a leak test raise it.
